t:
Section 7(h)(1)(C)(iii) of the Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act (43 U.S.C. 1606(h)(1)(C)(iii)) is amended by inserting before the period at the end the following: “, notwithstanding an adoption, 
relinquishment, or termination of parental rights that may have altered or severed the legal relationship between the gift donor and recipient”.

fable.w: This section amends the Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act to clarify that gift transfers of settlement common stock remain permitted despite adoption or termination of parental rights. It concerns private stock transfers between individuals, not any federal decision involving consultation, comment, hearings, advisory bodies, or a right to sue. The mention of Alaska Natives (an outside group) might tempt a Yes, but no participation process in a federal decision is created.
fable.s:
notwithstanding an adoption, 
relinquishment, or termination of parental rights that may have altered or severed the legal relationship between the gift donor and recipient

qwen_block.w: This section is a technical amendment to a statute regarding the legal definition of relationships for gift purposes. It does not establish any process for public comment, consultation with outside entities, advisory boards, or hearings. It merely clarifies the scope of existing legal relationships.
qwen_block.s: Section 7(h)(1)(C)(iii) of the Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act (43 U.S.C. 1606(h)(1)(C)(iii)) is amended by inserting before the period at the end the following: “, notwithstanding an adoption, relinquishment, or termination of parental rights that may have altered or severed the legal relationship between the gift donor and recipient”.

opus.w: This is a technical amendment to the rules on who may receive gifts of Alaska Native settlement stock. It creates no consultation, advisory body, hearing, comment period, rulemaking authority, or right to sue. A reference to Alaska Natives alone does not cross the federal boundary into participation in a federal decision.
opus.s:
notwithstanding an adoption, 
relinquishment, or termination of parental rights that may have altered or severed the legal relationship between the gift donor and recipient
opus.b: 1. **Tempting-but-wrong reading:** The section amends the Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act, and mentions of Alaska Natives and Native corporations might suggest tribal consultation. That reading fails. The amendment only clarifies who counts as an eligible gift recipient of settlement stock, even when an adoption or termination of parental rights has changed the family relationship. No outside party is consulted, given a hearing, given a comment period, or given a right to sue over a federal decision. No rulemaking is authorized either.

qwen_chat.w: The section amends a specific provision of the Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act regarding the legal relationship between gift donors and recipients. It does not create any mechanism for outside parties to consult with, advise, or participate in federal decision-making. There are no hearings, comment periods, advisory boards with non-federal members, or rights to sue mentioned. The mention of private parties is purely definitional within the context of the amendment.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the text mentions "gift donor and recipient," it involves private parties. However, the text is merely amending a definition or condition regarding legal relationships for the purpose of a specific settlement act provision. It does not establish a process for consultation, comment, hearing, or advisory input from outside parties into a federal decision-making process. It is a substantive legal amendment, not a procedural participation mechanism.
